plan_review.notes: Adversarial-style rubber-duck review of the stateless, marker-based, review-gated design. 4 blocking concerns: (1) no auto-trigger on review-issue close -> added issues:[closed,reopened] trigger + concurrency group; (2) any closed state treated as approval -> gated on state_reason==completed vs not_planned rejection; (3) no pin to reviewed file revision -> added epicContentHash + reviewHashMarker drift detection; (4) no concurrency control -> added concurrency group (group: epic-create). 3 non-blocking concerns addressed: node.id charset validation, description/review field type validation, duplicate epic_id across a multi-file batch (assertUniqueEpicIds). One non-blocking suggestion (CODEOWNERS entry for docs/knowledge/epics/**) consciously deferred as a separate governance change out of this tasks scope; noted in the PR/handoff. All fixes were refinements to the same core design (stateless marker-based issues, no control-plane file) rather than a different architecture, so plan_divergence=minor.

rounds.notes: Shell injection via workflow_dispatch epic_path interpolated into run: blocks; state_reason:null on a closed issue treated as approval; a stale not_planned rejection permanently blocking a revised (different-hash) plan.

Diagnostic promised a fresh review issue could be filed for a revised plan but no mechanism existed to create one (marker was epic-scoped, not hash-scoped); resolved by refactoring reviewMarker to embed the content hash directly so a revision automatically gets its own new review issue.

fetchEpicIssues embedded a redundant per_page=100 query param that paginate() also appends unconditionally; removed from the caller. A second, low-severity note (issues:closed firing for every repo issue close, filtered only via job-level if:) was accepted as a known limitation given low expected volume and the 10-minute job timeout.
Confirmation round: no remaining validated findings across all review categories.
